theorem_title: A nonempty finite family of weights has an attained minimum
natural_language_statement: Let m be a natural number with m ≥ 1, let w : Fin m → ℝ, and let X be real. If X < w(i) for every i, then there exists a real wstar with X < wstar, wstar ≤ w(i) for every i, and wstar = w(i) for some i.
explanation: The finite index set Fin m is nonempty because m ≥ 1. Choose an index where w attains its minimum on this set. Its value is no greater than any other value, is attained by construction, and is strictly above X by the assumed bound at the chosen index.
